newsitem.title: USA: Sluggish U.S. crude business yields steady prices.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish U.S. crude business yields steady prices.

text.p: U.S. crude prices gained slightly Friday morning in a sluggishly traded session.
Cash dealers said little business was seen as many market players were out of their offices at an assortment of industry functions.
Outright prices attracted technical buying, moving through resistance levels to peg gains of nearly 10 cents at $21.35-45 a barrel for June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Domestic grades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at three cents under to even with benchmark WTI, with no fresh trades seen.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire lost some 10 cents to talk at 70-60 cents under the marker. Midland/WTI tracked a few cents off Thursday's value at 39-35 cents under June WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island were steady as well, each pegged around $1.55 under marker crude.
The only trades confirmed were for June Postings Plus at $2.00, two cents lower than last deals Thursday.

Traders said sweet barrels in the Gulf continued to find pressure from wide arbitrage spreads between prompt Brent-WTI. Current numbers put June Brent-WTI around $1.70-75, and July Brent-WTI at the same range.
Wider arb numbers improves the economics of bringing North Sea crudes to Gulf refiners.
